Antecedentes Clínicos:
Hipótesis diagnóstica: GONALGIA DER, OBS MENISCOPATIA LATERAL
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Fibrilación marginal del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral.
Menisco medial de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
No hay derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
Aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Mínimo aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
No hay otros hallazgos relevantes que consignar.
Impresión:
Fibrilación marginal del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
Discretos signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula

Regelrechte Artikulation am linken Kniegelenk. Nachweis einer nicht dislozierten Fraktur des medialen Tibiaplateaus mit vorwiegend horizontalem Frakturverlauf und vertikaler Komponente welche nach ventral bis an die Vorderhorn-Wurzel des Innenmeniskus heranreicht (8/13 oder 5/7). Angrenzendes Bone Bruise im medialen Tibiaplateau. Ansonsten kein weiteres Knochenmarksödem.

Die Patella zentriert stehend. Mit nur geringen oberflächlichen chondralen Läsionen (z. B. 7/10). An der Trochlea keine tief greifende Chondropathie.

Femorotibial erhaltener Knorpelbelag ohne tief greifende Chondropathie. Die Menisken sind intakt. Vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband intakt. Kollateralbänder ebenfalls intakt. Geringer Reizzustand des MCL am tibialen Ansatz. Kein Gelenkerguss. Synovialis schlank. Kein Gelenkerguss. Keine vermehrte Flüssigkeit in den Sehnenscheiden. Die miterfassten muskulären und tendinösen Strukturen stellen sich unauffällig dar. Geringe Flüssigkeitseinlagerungen in die Subcutis.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinitis.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Transformación quística parcial del LCA, sin signos de rotura. LCP y ligamentos colaterales dentro
de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones
significativas.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial difusa.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital
suprarrotuliano.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Condropatía rotuliana superficial.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal.
Signos de un síndrome de fricción de la banda iliotibial.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, hallazgo inespecífico, podría
representar fenómenos de mal alineamiento rotuliano

Flächige Ausdünnung des Gelenkknorpels in der medialen femorotibialen Belastungszone ohne höhergradige oder vollschichtige Läsion, passend zu einer beginnenden medialen Gonarthrose.  Ligamentäre Strukturen intakt. Rundliche, zystisch imponierende Struktur pararezessal an der Basis des Außenmeniskusvorderhorns, DD Meniskusganglion (3, 103). Diskrete Signalanhebung innerhalb des Hinterhorns des Innenmeniskus (5, 6), a.e. vereinbar mit mukoiden Veränderungen. Im Übrigen unauffällige Signalgebung.

Findings: There is no significant knee effusion. There is a horizontal undersurface tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a fragment flipped towards the midline. Normal lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Normal tibiofemoral and trochlear articular cartilage. Fissuring of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage is noted.  Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Flipped tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Focal patellar articular cartilage fissuring.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED]. Pain is at the anterior aspect.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Small tricompartmental marginal osteophyte formation.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal cartilage fissuring at the peripheral margin of the medial tibial plateau with associated subchondral edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade and full thickness fissuring of the lateral patellar facet with subchondral cystic change/edema. Signal heterogeneity of the trochlear cartilage.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Focal edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Mild tricompartmental osteoarthritis, most significant within the patellofemoral compartment with focal fissuring of the lateral patellar facet.
2.	Focal edema within the lateral Hoffa's fat pad suggestive of lateral patellofemoral maltracking.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right-sided knee pain.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, consistent with extensive complex tearing. The anterior horn shows intrasubstance degeneration without tear. The posterior root is barely perceptible consistent with extensive complex tear. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body.

Barely perceptible posterior root of the lateral meniscus raising suspicion for complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. No lateral meniscal extrusion. 

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with intrasubstance ganglion formation. Slight anterior tibial translation.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament near the medial femoral condyle origin. The meniscotibial meniscal femoral component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact. The posterior oblique ligament is intact.

Fibular collateral ligament is intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis of the lateral femoral condylar attachment, without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 15 mm, at the upper limit of normal. No patellofemoral subluxation.

There is focal full thickness cartilage denuding at the patellar apex with fissuring of articular cartilage at the patellar apex and extending along the medial patellar facet. There is diffuse full-thickness cartilage denuding throughout the weightbearing aspect of the medial femorotibial compartment with subchondral sclerosis. There is mild to moderate lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Prominent non-marginal lateral femoral condylar osteophyte.

Trace knee joint fluid. Subcutaneous edema along the lateral and posterior aspects of the knee and proximal calf. There is generalized atrophy of the regional musculature which maybe on the basis of deconditioning. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Extensive complex tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion and tricompartment chondrosis as pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment, consistent with severe medial compartment predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.
2. Suspected complex tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus without lateral meniscal extrusion.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Borderline lateralization of the tibial tubercle which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
6. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with slight anterior tibial translation.

Runde signalarme intraossäre Struktur DD Enostom interkondylär (5/16) sowie der medialen proximalen Tibia (5/14). VKB sowie der KB intakt. Und regelrecht einsetzend. Menisken mit geringem mukoiden Signal, kein Rissnachweis. Kollateralbänder intakt. Diskrete ödematöse Veränderungen im Verlauf des durchgängig abgrenzbaren MPFL (4/9-11). Kein Chondropathiesignal. Kein bone bruise. Kein Gelenkerguss. kleine synoviale Zyste angrenzend an das anterolaterale Tibiaplateau (3/119). Regelrechter Flow-void der miterfassten Gefäße. Muskeln sowie deren Ansätze regelrecht signalgebend. Physiologisches Knochenmarksignal. Sulcuswinkel 155°. Keine axiale Patellaverschiebung. Caton-Deschamps-Index: 1,3.

Erhaltene Artikulation im linken Knie. Deutliche T2 Signalanhebungen intraossär in der medialen Femurkondyle sowie etwas geringer auch subchondral im medialen Tibiaplateau. Ansonsten unauffälliges Knochenmarkssignal. Geringe oberflächliche Chondropathie retropatellar (z.B. 7/11). Vollschichtig, flächige Chondropathie im medialen femorotibialen Kompartiment (z. B. 4/17). In der medialen Femurkondyle kleinzystische Veränderungen (4/17). Im lateralen femorotibialen Kompartiment keine wesentliche Chondropathie. Außenmeniskushinterhorn geringe signalalteriert. Kein Nachweis einer Rissbildung. Der Innenmeniskus ausgeprägt mukoide T2 signalalteriert und aufgefasert mit Extrusion in der Pars intermedia und Hinterhorn bei komplexer Rissbildung mit unter anderem vollständiger radiärer Komponente nahe der Hinterhornwurzel (z. B. 3/98). Kleine parameniskale Zysten (z. B. 4/22). Kreuzbänder und Kollateralbänder intakt. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Synovia verdickt und unscharf, DD bei Reiz Synovialitis. Umgebende Muskulatur und Subkutis unauffällig.
